# AGENTS.md - seaPilot

## Product
seaPilot is a case workspace for e-commerce customer service (CS) agents.
One case can span many conversations and many CS agents.
The AI reads stored case data, finds what changed since the last contact,
and drafts a reply and a next action. A CS agent approves every reply and
every action before it is sent or executed.

WHAT we build: docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md (scenes, triage rules, cut-line).
HOW the demo runs: docs/DEMO-RUNBOOK.md. Topology: docs/Architecture.md.
Exact demo data: prompts/04-demo-data.md. Build tasks: prompts/02-build-tasks.md.

## Current stack and scope
- Two independent Next.js App Router apps with strict TypeScript: `apps/customer`
  (port 3000) and `apps/customer-service` (port 3001).
- Tailwind CSS and official shadcn/ui components in `packages/ui`; shared Zod
  schemas in `packages/contracts` and in-memory fixtures in `packages/demo`.
- `apps/api`: Hono on Node 20+, strict TypeScript, run with `tsx`, port 4000.
- PostgreSQL 16 in Docker (`docker-compose.yml` at the repo root), Drizzle ORM
  with the `postgres` driver, migrations in `apps/api/drizzle`. All data access
  goes through a `CaseStore` interface in `apps/api/src/store`.
- OpenAI Responses API with function tools, server side only, model from `OPENAI_MODEL`.
- Both web apps will call the API through `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE`. `packages/demo`
  stays only as a fallback for UI development.
- Exposed for the demo with: `cloudflared tunnel --url [REDACTED URL]
- Vitest plus the Node usage-recorder suite. Both run through `pnpm test`.
- The user explicitly requested Next.js, two sites and shadcn. Preserve this
  implemented frontend; the incoming Vite/no-component-library scaffold plan
  does not authorize replacing it.

For frontend work, read `docs/FRONTEND-BASE.md` for commands and scope,
`DESIGN.md` for tokens and components, and `docs/FRONTEND-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md`
for delivery status. For backend work, read `docs/Architecture.md` and
`prompts/02-build-tasks.md`: they preserve main's Hono/PostgreSQL/Drizzle/tunnel
integration plan, not implemented services. Adapt their one-package/Vite paths
to this workspace before implementation. Do not replace the frontend or deploy
without a new user instruction.

## Commands (run from repo root)
- install: `pnpm install`
- dev: `pnpm dev` (Customer 3000, Customer Service 3001)
- build: `pnpm build` (both independent Next.js builds)
- typecheck: `pnpm typecheck`
- lint: `pnpm lint`
- test: `pnpm test` (Vitest and Node recorder tests)
- reset: local preview Reset control (no backend reset exists yet)
Run typecheck, lint and test before you say a task is done.
Database, migration and tunnel commands in the integration plan are not available
in the current package scripts.

## Hard rules
1. The repo is PUBLIC. Never commit secrets. Keys live only in `.env` (git-ignored).
   Keep `.env.example` with names only. DATABASE_URL and POSTGRES_PASSWORD are env too;
   a dev-only default may appear in docker-compose.yml.
2. When backend integration is implemented, OPENAI_API_KEY is server-only. The
   web bundle never contains a secret. The planned demo token stays in sessionStorage.
3. The AI never writes to the database. It calls tools; the API validates
   the arguments with Zod and runs the query.
4. Every fact shown to CS has a source: "customer", "system" or "unverified".
5. No reply or action runs without CS approval. Record every approval and
   every result in case_events. Never show "done" before the action succeeds.
6. Never ask the customer for information that is already in the case.
7. Stay inside the demo scope. Ask before adding a new dependency.
8. Responses API: tools use the Responses API format. Do not send temperature
   or top_p. Read the model name from env OPENAI_MODEL.
9. Small commits with clear messages, with the task id: `feat(T04): agent loop`.
   Commits are authored by the team git identity; no Co-authored-by lines.
10. After each task, append to docs/codex-log.md: task id, start and end time,
    what you built, files changed, tests added, problems found.
11. Every developer must record every Codex prompt used for this project.
    Use the shared `.codex/hooks.json`; run `node scripts/codex-usage/cli.mjs install`
    after cloning, then review/trust the project and hooks via Codex CLI `/hooks`.
    `.codex-usage/events/` contains PUBLIC, redacted prompt/tool evidence and must
    be included with the related work in Git. Run `node scripts/codex-usage/cli.mjs report`
    to regenerate the shared report. Never disable or bypass recording for project work.
    Fix failed prompt recording before retrying. For activity outside hook coverage,
    add a truthful manual entry; never invent automatic evidence. Keep secrets out
    of prompts and logs. See docs/codex-usage.md.
12. CORS on the API: exact-origin allowlist from env CORS_ORIGINS, never `*`.
    Handle OPTIONS before auth. `GET /files/*` and `GET /api/health` need no token.

## Planned backend data model
customers, orders, order_items, shipments (parcel_code, status, updated_at),
cases (id = code e.g. CS001, status, assignee, order_id, title),
conversations (id, case_id nullable, customer_id, channel, opened_at, mode "human"|"auto"),
messages (id, conversation_id, role, text, created_at),
evidence (id, case_id nullable, conversation_id, type, path, source, created_at),
case_events (id, case_id, type, actor, payload json, created_at),
tasks (id, case_id, team, status, evidence_ids json, created_at).
Ids are the fixture strings from prompts/04-demo-data.md (CS001, CONV1, EV1 ...);
new rows get short random ids with the same prefix. Case status: open ->
waiting_customer -> waiting_ops -> resolved. Team id "operations", label "Warehouse Ops".

## Backend integration decisions from main
- First case: approving a reply in a conversation with no case creates the case,
  links the conversation, attaches pending evidence, writes case_created.
- Change detection baseline: every reply_sent event stores `shipment_snapshot`
  (parcel_code -> status). changes_since_last_contact = last snapshot vs now.
- Handover: POST link-conversation sets case.assignee = actor and writes
  assignee_changed. Switching "Signed in as" in the UI changes nothing in data.
- Agent failure: API returns `{ ok: false, error, suggestion: null }`; UI disables
  approve buttons. No error flag inside AgentSuggestion.
- Scene 3 reply is approved only after the escalation succeeds.

## Done means
- typecheck, lint and tests pass
- the frontend demo still runs after its local Reset control; verify backend reset once implemented
- no secret in the diff
- docs/codex-log.md updated
# seaPilot API (T02–T04)

Hono + PostgreSQL 16, with storage behind `CaseStore`. Requires Node 20.12+
(the workspace frontend may require a newer Node release), pnpm 10.28.2 and Docker.

From the repository root:

1. Run `pnpm install`.
2. Copy `apps/api/.env.example` to `apps/api/.env`. Set `DATABASE_URL`,
   `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `DEMO_RESET_TOKEN`; optionally set `PORT` and `CORS_ORIGINS`.
   The database URL must match the Compose password, local port 5432 and database
   `seapilot`. Compose has a local demo password default; set your own in `.env`.
   The agent needs server-only `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL`; other routes and
   mocked tests work without a key.
3. Run `pnpm db:up`, `pnpm db:migrate`, then `pnpm db:reset`.
4. Run `pnpm dev` for all three apps, or `pnpm dev:api` for just the API.

API and database bind to loopback. The API defaults to `[REDACTED URL]
`pnpm tunnel` exposes that API when explicitly run; this task does not start it.

| Route | Authentication | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/health` | Public | `{ ok: true, time, db: "up" or "down" }` |
| `GET /files/demo/parcel_a.jpg` | Public | Labeled placeholder JPEG |
| `GET /files/demo/parcel_b_open.jpg` | Public | Labeled placeholder JPEG |
| `GET /files/<name>` | Public | File in `public/`, otherwise `data/uploads/` |
| `POST /api/demo/reset` | `x-demo-token` | Start fixtures, clock day 0 |
| `POST /api/demo/jump?to=demo2` | `x-demo-token` | After Demo 1 fixtures, clock day 0 |
| `POST /api/demo/advance-day` | `x-demo-token` | B delivered and audited at current time, then clock +1 day |
| `GET /api/cases/:id/context` | Public demo API | Case, recent messages/events, evidence, open tasks and shipment changes |
| `GET /api/orders/:id/shipments` | Public demo API | Order and parcels with their items and current statuses |
| `POST /api/agent/suggest` | Public demo API | Body `{ conversation_id }`; envelope `{ ok, suggestion, error? }` |

The token must equal `DEMO_RESET_TOKEN`; missing server configuration fails closed.
CORS accepts exact origins from `CORS_ORIGINS`, comma separated. Defaults are
localhost and 127.0.0.1 on ports 3000 and 3001. Preflight runs before authentication.

The demo clock is process-local memory. Restarting the API starts its clock at day 0;
use the HTTP reset when it is running to reset both database and clock together.
The CLI shares the reset implementation but cannot change another process's clock.
Demo control requests in one server process are serialized. Database resets use one
TRUNCATE statement and inserts in a transaction; shipment changes and audit events
also commit together. Advance-day audits every unresolved DH001 case.

`CaseStore.get(table, id)` and `list(table, partialRowFilter)` support all ten tables;
reads return ISO timestamp strings. Named writes validate with the separate Zod row
contracts. `transaction` supports atomic multi-step operations. Linking also attaches
pending evidence, changes assignee and records both audit events. Future routes must
require CS approval before calling writes for replies or actions.

The fixture document leaves Sam's item, secondary emails, and some IDs unspecified;
those are explicit demo placeholders in `seed.ts`. No expected-delivery column was
added to the exact ERD. Both parcel images are labeled illustrations, not real photos.

## Checks

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm test` run from the root. Tests intentionally
do not auto-load `.env`: integration tests print a clear skip when `DATABASE_URL`
is unset, and otherwise truncate all ten tables in the selected database. Use only
a disposable demo/test database. After migrating it, run the complete suite with:

```sh
node --env-file=apps/api/.env -e 'const {spawnSync}=require("node:child_process"); process.exit(spawnSync("pnpm",["test"],{stdio:"inherit",env:process.env}).status??1)'
```

Then `pnpm db:reset` restores Start. Migration changes are generated with
`pnpm --filter @seapilot/api db:generate`; commit the SQL and Drizzle metadata together.
The existing frontend remains on its local fixtures until a later integration task.

## Agent tools and trial script

The Responses API uses the three read-only functions in `src/ai/tools.ts`, with
Zod-validated arguments/results and JSON schemas. The official `openai` SDK stays
on v6 to preserve this API's Node 20 support. Unresolved cases for the same
customer start at 0.5; matching the order gives 0.9, plus 0.05 per unique matching
keyword up to 1.0. If no order is supplied, the customer's most recent order is used.
Text alone cannot search other customers. Conversation summaries are attributed
message excerpts. A missing reply snapshot produces no inferred shipment changes.

The agent reads `prompts/03-runtime-prompt.md`, permits at most six tool calls across
the entire run and validation retry, and applies one 30-second deadline to the run.
Invalid JSON/schema output gets one repair attempt. Failure always returns a null
suggestion; only validated suggestions are audited as `ai_suggestion` for an already
linked conversation. Replies, linking and actions still require separate CS approval.
Function calls and reasoning items are preserved as described in the
[official Responses function-calling guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling).

`pnpm try:suggest` loads `apps/api/.env`, resets the selected database to After Demo 1,
advances a day, creates only the returning conversation and M2 customer message, and
prints the real-model suggestion envelope as JSON. It exits with an explicit error
before connecting or changing data when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is missing. With a key,
this script intentionally replaces demo data; its clock is separate from a running
API process, as with `db:reset`. The automated script check forces an empty key and
does not contact OpenAI.

## Conversation continuity and approvals

Workspace routes are public (no demo token); only `/api/demo/*` controls require
`x-demo-token`. JSON writes validate bodies with Zod and return `{ ok, data }` or
`{ ok: false, error }`. Missing records return 404, invalid input 400, and blocked
links/replies 409.

- `POST /api/conversations` — `{ customer_id }`; creates an unlinked chat.
- `GET /api/conversations?customer_id=CUST001` — filtered list (omit the filter for all).
- `GET /api/conversations/:id` — conversation, messages, evidence, and `case` summary.
- `POST /api/conversations/:id/messages` — `{ role: "customer", text }`.
- `POST /api/upload` — multipart `conversation_id` and `file` (JPEG/PNG/WebP,
  up to 10 MiB), or JSON `{ conversation_id, seed: "parcel_a" | "parcel_b_open" }`.
  Uploaded filenames are generated; bytes live in `apps/api/data/uploads`.
  Both forms create customer evidence with the conversation's current case ID.
- `POST /api/cases/:id/link-conversation` — `{ conversation_id, actor }`.
  Attaches pending evidence and records the handover. Repeating the same link does
  nothing, even if another actor retries. Cross-customer/relink attempts fail.
- `POST /api/approve` — `{ conversation_id, kind: "reply", text, actor, title? }`.
  `title` is required when creating a first case. Uses the latest customer order,
  assigns the next `CSnnn`, and saves the approved message plus shipment snapshot.
- `POST /api/approve` — `{ conversation_id, kind: "action", actor,
  action: { type: "escalate_to_ops", reason, evidence_ids } }`.
  Evidence must belong to the case. Creates one operations task per case, updates
  status and records `action_executed` in one transaction. Repeated/concurrent
  approvals return the existing task. Failure rolls back and records `action_failed`.
  A case with an escalation suggestion cannot send a reply until its task exists.
- `GET /api/cases/:id` — case, events, evidence and tasks.

The agent includes pending conversation evidence and the latest order ID in its
initial context, and requests `reasoning.encrypted_content` on every Responses call,
including tool continuations and validation retries. No mock fallback is enabled in
production.

Run the full test suite safely using disposable, migrated PostgreSQL databases:

```sh
pnpm --filter @seapilot/api exec tsx scripts/test-isolated.ts
```

Run the same three-scene story with actual curl requests and a mocked Responses
client (the API key is forced empty):

```sh
pnpm --filter @seapilot/api exec tsx scripts/verify-continuity.ts
```

Both commands load the existing API `.env` without printing it and require the
configured PostgreSQL role to create/drop a temporary database. They never reset
the configured demo database. The curl harness serves the app on an ephemeral
loopback port and closes only its own server; port 4000 is left alone.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { mkdir, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import type { Hono } from 'hono';
import { z } from 'zod';
import { AgentSuggestionSchema, type DbTable } from '@seapilot/contracts';
import type { CaseStore } from './store/CaseStore';

const id = z.string().trim().min(1);
const actionSchema = AgentSuggestionSchema.shape.proposed_action.unwrap().extend({ evidence_ids: z.array(id).min(1) });
const approveSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('kind', [
  z.object({ conversation_id: id, kind: z.literal('reply'), text: id, title: id.optional(), actor: id }).strict(),
  z.object({ conversation_id: id, kind: z.literal('action'), action: actionSchema, actor: id }).strict(),
]);
export class RequestError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string, public status: 400 | 404 | 409 = 400) { super(message); }
}
async function required<K extends DbTable>(store: CaseStore, table: K, key: string) {
  const row = await store.get(table, key);
  if (!row) throw new RequestError(`${table} not found`, 404);
  return row;
}
const uploadRoot = new URL('../data/uploads/', import.meta.url);

export function registerWorkspace(app: Hono, store: CaseStore, now: () => string) {

    const body = z.object({ customer_id: id }).strict().parse(await c.req.json());
    await required(store, 'customers', body.customer_id);
    return c.json({ ok: true, data: await store.createConversation({ ...body, case_id: null, channel: 'chat', mode: 'human', opened_at: now() }) }, 201);
  });

  });

    const [messages, evidence, summary] = await Promise.all([
      store.list('messages', { conversation_id: conversation.id }), store.list('evidence', { conversation_id: conversation.id }),
      conversation.case_id ? store.get('cases', conversation.case_id) : null,
    ]);
    return c.json({ ok: true, data: { conversation, messages: messages.sort((a, b) => a.created_at.localeCompare(b.created_at)), evidence, case: summary } });
  });
  app.post('/api/conversations/:id/messages', async c => {
    const body = z.object({ role: z.literal('customer'), text: id }).strict().parse(await c.req.json());
    const conversation = await required(store, 'conversations', c.req.param('id'));
    return c.json({ ok: true, data: await store.addMessage({ ...body, conversation_id: conversation.id, actor: conversation.customer_id, created_at: now() }) }, 201);
  });
  app.post('/api/upload', async c => {
    let path: string;
    let conversation_id: string;
    let saved: URL | undefined;
    if (c.req.header('content-type')?.startsWith('multipart/form-data')) {
      const body = z.object({ conversation_id: id, file: z.instanceof(File).refine(file => file.size > 0 && file.size <= 10 * 1024 * 1024, 'Expected a file up to 10 MiB') }).strict().parse(await c.req.parseBody());
      conversation_id = body.conversation_id;
      await required(store, 'conversations', conversation_id);
      const extension = ({ 'image/jpeg': 'jpg', 'image/png': 'png', 'image/webp': 'webp' } as Record<string, string>)[body.file.type];
      if (!extension) throw new RequestError('Expected a JPEG, PNG or WebP image');
      const name = `${randomUUID()}.${extension}`;
      saved = new URL(name, uploadRoot);
      await mkdir(uploadRoot, { recursive: true });
      await writeFile(saved, Buffer.from(await body.file.arrayBuffer()), { flag: 'wx' });
      path = `/files/${name}`;
    } else {
      const body = z.object({ conversation_id: id, seed: z.enum(['parcel_a', 'parcel_b_open']) }).strict().parse(await c.req.json());
      conversation_id = body.conversation_id;
      path = `/files/demo/${body.seed}.jpg`;
    }
    try {
      const evidence = await store.transaction(async tx => {
        const conversation = await required(tx, 'conversations', conversation_id);
        const evidence = await tx.addEvidence({ conversation_id, case_id: conversation.case_id, type: 'image', path, source: 'customer', created_at: now() });
        if (conversation.case_id) await tx.addEvent({ case_id: conversation.case_id, type: 'evidence_added', actor: conversation.customer_id, payload: { evidence_id: evidence.id
